newsitem.title: UK: FKI allows Newman Tonks bid to lapse.
newsitem.headline: FKI allows Newman Tonks bid to lapse.

text.p: British engineering group FKI Plc said on Wednesday it was allowing its hostile bid for Newman Tonks to lapse after it decided not to raise its offer, which valued the British building products group at 195.7 million pounds ($317 million).
FKI's decision came two days after U.S.-based Ingersoll-Rand launched a surprise agreed cash offer which valued Newman Tonks at around 230 million pounds.
FKI said it was supplied confidential information by Newman Tonks after Ingersoll-Rand offered to pay 175 pence for each Newman Tonks share.

"Having carefully studied the confidential information supplied to us, it is clear that a higher offer would not create sufficient value for our shareholders and we have therefore decided to lapse our offer," FKI's chairman Jeff Whalley said in a statement.
FKI also ruled out a proposed rights issue of two for 13 existing shares which would have helped it to raise a maximum of 152.4 million pounds to help finance the acquisition.

Newman Tonk shareholders who had already tendered forms of acceptance in respect of the offer would be released from such acceptances and their documents of title would be returned to them over the next few days, FKI said.
